**Org standard**

- The backend runs on **Bun** by explicit architectural decision, not merely implementation convenience.
- **ADR-002 — “Backend service stack and runtime”** is **Accepted** and specifies Bun as the production/container runtime: `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-002-backend-service-stack-and-runtime.md`.
- Rationale recorded in the ADR:
  - Align production with **Bun’s performance and emerging ecosystem**.
  - Pair Hono with a Bun-based deployment for the REST API and in-process MCP endpoint.
  - Keep application code compatible with Bun’s Node-style runtime rather than depending on Bun-only APIs.
  - Node.js was considered and rejected for the container runtime; Express/Fastify were also rejected as more Node-centric alternatives.
- Trade-off acknowledged: deployments must target Bun-compatible environments, so teams standardized on pure Node images may need changes.

**Codebase (tool-grounded)**

- Backend instructions require **Bun for the container/on-prem entrypoint, not Node**: `apps/backend/AGENTS.md`.
- The production Docker stage uses `oven/bun:1.3.11-alpine` and starts the service with:
  - `bun run apps/backend/src/server.ts`
  - `apps/backend/Dockerfile`
- Node is still installed in the dependency-build stage because `pnpm` is treated as a Node CLI and may stall when run through Bun. That is build tooling compatibility, not a change in the production runtime.
- The backend README likewise names Bun as its container/runtime target: `apps/backend/README.md`.

**Org standard — FalkorDB is the default** for local development and the recommended production graph engine.

- **ADR:** [ADR-010 — OpenCypher Graph DB and FalkorDB as Default](.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-010-opencypher-graph-db-falkordb-default.md), accepted 2026-03-05.
- **Why FalkorDB:**
  - Open-source and avoids Neo4j’s Enterprise requirement for multi-database tenancy.
  - Simple Docker/Bolt setup for fast local iteration.
  - Native tenant isolation via multiple graphs per instance; the ADR cites support for 10,000+ isolated graphs.
  - Fits the approved unified tenancy model: database-per-tenant on a shared instance, or instance-per-tenant.

**Supported engines**

- **FalkorDB** — default; supports database-per-tenant and instance-per-tenant.
- **Neo4j** — database-per-tenant requires Enterprise; instance-per-tenant supported.
- **Memgraph** — database-per-tenant requires Enterprise; instance-per-tenant supported.
- **Amazon Neptune** — instance-per-tenant only.
- **Neo4j Community** — instance-per-tenant only; no database-per-tenant mode.

The ADR standardizes on a single Bolt-compatible driver and configurable `GRAPH_DB_URI`, so deployments can select a supported OpenCypher engine while preserving the tenancy model.

**Org standard:** **Terraform** is the infrastructure-as-code standard.

- **Decision record:** [ADR-013 — “Switch infra from Pulumi to Terraform”](.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-013-switch-infra-from-pulumi-to-terraform.md) — accepted 2026-03-17.
- **Previous alternative:** Pulumi.
- **Why Terraform was chosen:**
  - Broader ecosystem support for providers, modules, tooling, and CI.
  - Better interoperability for self-hosting across Railway, AWS, GCP, and Azure.
  - Customers already using Pulumi can consume Terraform modules, avoiding a dependency on Pulumi for the core infrastructure.
  - A single Terraform source of truth avoids split-brain infrastructure definitions.

ADR-013 specifies Railway + Neon production infrastructure under `infra/`, with reusable modules in `infra/module/ctxpipe/`, and remote Terraform state stored in Cloudflare R2 via the S3 backend.

**Org standard**

- Railway hosted compute runs in **`us-east4-eqdc4a` (Virginia / US East)**.
- The database is Neon’s transaction pooler in **`aws-us-east-1`**, so this placement keeps application compute close to SQL and avoids the prior transpacific round trip from Singapore.
- Rationale: org-scoped database requests are short transactions; the previous Singapore placement added roughly **~200 ms RTT per network hop**, producing about **~1 second** of latency per database interaction.
- This is an accepted architectural decision: **ADR-029 — “Railway compute in US East next to Neon”**: `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-029-railway-us-east-next-to-neon.md`.

**Codebase / operational caveat**

- Region configuration is intended to come from `var.railway_regions`, defaulting to one replica in `us-east4-eqdc4a`.
- Because Railway Terraform provider 0.6.x does not reliably update `multiRegionConfig`, **region changes are applied through Railway GraphQL plus redeploy**, rather than Terraform’s update path.

No. **AgentMemory is no longer part of the current local agent memory architecture.**

## Org standard

- **Current approach:** Markdown-only, Git-native durable memory under `.ai/memory/`.
- **Navigation:** root and per-directory `index.md` files.
- **Capture model:** host lifecycle hooks run `ctxpipe memory capture observe|summary`, which redact/classify and append *candidate* events under gitignored `.ai/memory/events/`.
- **Promotion:** agents—not hooks—promote useful candidates into durable Markdown such as:
  - `lessons-learned.md`
  - `glossary.md`
  - `product-context.md`
  - `decisions/`
  - `PRDs/`
  - `sessions/`
  and update the relevant index.
- **Explicitly not used:** no local search daemon, no hydrated AgentMemory cache, and no hosted-embeddings recall path.

**ADR:** [ADR-024 — Markdown-only local memory with candidate-first capture](.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-024-markdown-only-local-memory-capture.md) is **accepted** and explicitly **supersedes ADR-021**.

## Codebase (tool-grounded)

- `AGENTS.md` states that durable memory is Markdown-only under `.ai/memory/`, navigated by `index.md`; hooks only append gitignored candidates and must not auto-write durable ADRs.
- The earlier AgentMemory integration is documented in [ADR-021](.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-021-local-agent-memory-agentmemory-hybrid-mcp-proxy.md), but that ADR is marked **superseded by ADR-024**.

So, treat any `AgentMemory` runtime/MCP/proxy material as historical context from the superseded design—not the recommended current setup.

**Org standard / current decision**

- **ADR-015 — “Docker Compose profiles and small-scale container deploy”** is the current, **accepted** decision:  
  `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-015-docker-compose-profiles-and-small-scale-deploy.md`
- **ADR-004 — “Local development with Docker Compose”** is **superseded** and should not be treated as the current authority:  
  `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-004-local-development-docker-compose.md`

**Local development today**

- Compose is organized around a single root `docker-compose.yml` with profiles.
- Run **`pnpm dev:infra`** for the **`infra`** profile:
  - PostgreSQL
  - FalkorDB
  - OpenTelemetry Collector
- Run application processes separately on the host with **`pnpm dev`**:
  - backend and UI run through the normal host development workflow (portless + Turbo)
  - codesearch runs in Docker via `scripts/codesearch-docker-dev.sh`, rather than as a Compose service
- This separation is intentional: Compose supplies backing infrastructure, while host tooling runs the actively developed applications. It avoids starting backend/UI twice and avoids requiring app secrets for infrastructure-only startup.

**Deployment distinction**

- **`pnpm start`** uses the **`deploy`** profile, which brings up production-oriented containers: migration job, backend, worker, UI, codesearch, plus the shared data services.
- The same Compose file supports both workflows, but local development should use `dev:infra` + `dev`, not the deploy profile.

**Cited ADR**

> `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-015-docker-compose-profiles-and-small-scale-deploy.md` — accepted; defines `infra` for host-based local development and `deploy` for small-scale/self-hosted production deployment.

**Architecture decisions governing the codesearch service**

- **ADR-008 — Codesearch service and Zoekt orchestration**  
  `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-008-codesearch-zoekt-orchestration.md`  
  Primary service architecture: Zoekt-backed search, repository/file APIs, and orchestration boundaries.

- **ADR-011 — Backend observability via OpenTelemetry and evlog**  
  `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-011-backend-observability-otel.md`  
  Governs observability shared by backend-facing services, including codesearch.

- **ADR-015 — Docker Compose profiles and small-scale container deploy**  
  `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-015-docker-compose-profiles-and-small-scale-deploy.md`  
  Governs local/deploy topology; codesearch is part of the Docker-based development and deployment profile.

- **ADR-027 — Size-based OpenWorkflow concurrency for single-instance codesearch**  
  `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-027-codesearch-openworkflow-concurrency.md`  
  Governs capacity and admission control: derive OpenWorkflow and indexer concurrency from the codesearch instance size, because codesearch is single-instance and stateful.

- **ADR-033 — Graph ontology v2: relation families, shared identities, deterministic connector extraction**  
  `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-033-graph-ontology-v2.md`  
  Governs the graph/SCIP-facing semantics used by codesearch and its extracted relationships.

**Related operational guidance**

- `AGENTS.md` explicitly scopes `apps/codesearch` to **Zoekt/SCIP orchestration, a read-only database, OpenAPI + Zod, and the manual Kubernetes ingest-memory gate**.
- The ADR index marks ADR-008 and ADR-027 as accepted; ADRs are the repository’s declared source of truth for high-level architecture.

**Org standard**

The `ui` app’s frontend stack is defined by **ADR-001: “Frontend UI app stack”**:

- **Runtime / framework:** TanStack Start with React and Vite
- **Styling:** Tailwind CSS v4
- **UI primitives:** React Aria components, installed/generated through the shadcn registry
- **Typography:** Geist and Geist Mono
- **Theme direction:** Tailwind teal primary palette with zinc grayscale
- **Component documentation:** Storybook
- **Testing:** Vitest with Testing Library

**Decision record:** [`.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-001-frontend-ui-app-stack.md`](.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-001-frontend-ui-app-stack.md) — accepted 2026-02-22.

A related structural decision is [ADR-009](.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-009-ui-src-folder-structure.md), which requires a feature-based `apps/ui/src` layout: thin routes, feature-owned code under `features/`, shared primitives in `components/ui/`, and app-wide composites/utilities in `components/` or `lib/`.

**Codebase (tool-grounded)**

- The app lives at `apps/ui`.
- Project guidance also identifies it as a **TanStack Start frontend using React Aria, Tailwind, Storybook, and Vitest**.

- **ORM:** Drizzle ORM, used with PostgreSQL.
- **Release channel:** **v1.x `beta`** for both `drizzle-orm` and `drizzle-kit` (pinned to the `beta` dist-tag rather than a fixed version).

**Architecture decisions**
- **ADR-002 — Backend service stack and runtime**: `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-002-backend-service-stack-and-runtime.md`  
  Establishes Drizzle ORM with PostgreSQL as the backend data layer.
- **ADR-003 — Drizzle ORM beta (v1.x)**: `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-003-drizzle-beta.md`  
  Accepts the Drizzle v1 beta channel and specifies `"beta"` for both packages.

**Org standard**

Store GitHub, Slack, Linear, and Notion integrations as typed rows in the unified **`connections`** table:

- IDs use the `con_*` prefix.
- Each row includes `org_id`, `type`, and type-specific `config` JSONB; secrets remain encrypted in `config` and must not be exposed from connector-list APIs.
- Supported relevant types: `github`, `slack`, `linear`, `notion`.
- Do **not** assume one integration per organization. Resolve explicitly by `connectionId` or repository scope.
- Do **not** add per-provider installation tables or revive `github_installations` / `forge_installations`.

Canonical decision: **[ADR-018 — Unified `connections` table](.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-018-unified-connections-table.md)**.

Provider-specific decisions:

| Provider | Storage / binding model | ADR |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub | Connection in `connections`; repository records refer to it through `github_connection_id`. | ADR-018 |
| Slack | `connections.type = slack`; encrypted bot credential in `connections.config`. Slack is intentional thread capture, not a continuous archive-style sync. | [ADR-025](.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-025-slack-connector-git-native-mirror.md) |
| Linear | `connections.type = linear`; OAuth credentials and target-repo sync binding live in `connections.config`. Scope is Git-native in `linear/config.yaml`, not a Postgres scopes/sync-targets table. | [ADR-022](.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-022-linear-connector-git-native-mirror.md) |
| Notion | `connections.type = notion`; encrypted OAuth credentials and target-repo sync binding live in `connections.config`. Scope is Git-native in `notion/config.yaml`, not `notion_sync_targets` or resource tables. | [ADR-023](.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-023-notion-connector-git-native-mirror.md) |

**Codebase (retrieval-grounded)**

- Repository guidance in `AGENTS.md` and `apps/backend/AGENTS.md` reinforces the unified `connections` model and says connector metadata endpoints must omit `config`.
- The accepted ADRs describe GitHub repositories referencing the connection by `github_connection_id`; newer Git-native connectors retain repository/branch/enabled setup binding in the connection’s JSONB configuration.

**Org standard — ADR-030, “Organization-owned MCP API keys”**  
Use an **organization-owned API key** for MCP clients that cannot complete browser OAuth: CI, headless agents, shared GUI environments, or hosts limited to static credentials.

- The key is bound to exactly one organization (`referenceId` is the organization ID), not to a member. It authenticates as an **org-service principal**, avoiding user impersonation and surviving membership changes.
- Mint organization keys in **Organization settings → API Keys** (admin/owner-controlled), not via the CLI.
- Use the generic MCP endpoint: `https://app.ctxpipe.ai/mcp`. An optional `?orgSlug=` must match the key’s bound organization.
- Preferred transport: `x-api-key: <key>`.
- Compatibility transport for Bearer-only MCP hosts (such as CodeRabbit): `Authorization: Bearer <key>` on **`/mcp` only**.
- API-key bearer fallback is deliberately MCP-scoped; organization keys do **not** authenticate organization REST endpoints.
- OAuth remains the default for interactive/laptop clients. The server resolves OAuth before treating an unrecognized opaque Bearer credential as an API key, so an API key cannot override a valid OAuth token.

**Codebase (tool-grounded)**  
- The accepted decision is `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-030-organization-owned-mcp-api-keys.md`.
- Hosted MCP documentation in `apps/docs/content/docs/(guide)/mcp/mcp-docs.mdx` matches ADR-030: it recommends API keys only when browser OAuth is unavailable, prefers `x-api-key`, permits Bearer compatibility on `/mcp`, and instructs clients to interpolate `CTXPIPE_API_KEY` rather than commit the secret.

**Org standard**

- **Logging:** Use **evlog**, not `console.*`, in `apps/backend`. Use `getLogger()` or `log` from `src/observability/logger.ts`.
- **Tracing:** Use **OpenTelemetry** with the Node SDK and an **OTLP/HTTP** trace exporter.
- **Configuration:** Observability is environment-driven:
  - `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` enables OTLP trace export.
  - `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT` enables evlog’s OTLP log drain; otherwise logs remain on stdout.
- **LLM tracing:** LangChain/LangGraph spans are emitted through Langfuse’s LangChain callback integration, passed via `runWithLangfuseContext` / `getLangfuseHandler()`. The backend does **not** use LangSmith or LangFuse-specific environment variables.
- **Multiple observability backends:** The backend emits each signal to one configured OTLP endpoint. Use an **OpenTelemetry Collector** for fan-out and destination-specific trace filtering—not application-side fan-out.
- **Startup ordering:** `parseEnv` → `initOtel` → `initEvlog` → `createApp`, so instrumentation registers before spans can be created.

**Architecture decision record**

- **ADR-011 — “Backend Observability via OpenTelemetry and evlog”**  
  `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-011-backend-observability-otel.md`  
  Status: accepted.
- The ADR establishes OTEL-first tracing, evlog structured logging, OTLP-based configuration, collector-managed fan-out, and the required initialization sequence.

**Codebase (tool-grounded)**

- The repository instructions explicitly require evlog in `apps/backend` and prohibit `console.*` for backend logging (`AGENTS.md`).

**Architecture decisions affecting the UI app**

1. **ADR-001 — Frontend UI app stack**  
   `.ai/memory/decisions/ADR-001-frontend-ui-app-stack.md`  
   - Establishes `apps/ui` as the frontend application.
   - **TanStack Start** (React + Vite) for runtime and routing.
   - **Tailwind CSS v4** with shared tokens in `apps/ui/src/styles.css`.
   - **Geist / Geist Mono**, teal primary palette, zinc grayscale.
   - **React Aria** primitives via the shadcn `@react-aria` registry.
   - **Storybook** and **Vitest + Testing Library** as baseline UI tooling.
   - Local development uses portless routing: `https://app.ctxpipe.localhost`, rather than assuming a fixed Vite port.

**Org standard**

- ADRs are the source of truth for high-level architectural decisions. For changes to the UI’s stack, tooling, or cross-cutting structure, consult `.ai/memory/decisions/` first.
- From the ADR set reviewed, **ADR-001 is the explicitly UI-focused decision**. Other ADRs may affect backend, infrastructure, connectors, or development workflows, but they are not established here as direct UI-app architecture decisions.

- **ADR-004 — Local development with Docker Compose**: superseded. The replacement ADR is **not identified** in the ADR index.
- **ADR-005 — LangGraph + LangChain integration**: superseded. The replacement ADR is **not identified** in the ADR index.
- **ADR-021 — Local agent memory with repo Markdown and AgentMemory hydrated cache**: superseded by **ADR-024 — Markdown-only local memory with candidate-first capture**.

Related but not superseded:
- **ADR-032 — Path-located graph edges** is **Accepted (amended by ADR-033)**, not marked superseded.

**Org standard**

The backend is governed primarily by these **accepted ADRs** in `.ai/memory/decisions/`:

| ADR | Decision | Backend impact |
|---|---|---|
| **ADR-002** | Backend service stack and runtime | Core standard: `apps/backend`, Hono + Bun, PostgreSQL/Neon + Drizzle, Better Auth, collocated Zod schemas, and MCP through `hono/mcp` sharing domain services with REST. |
| **ADR-003** | Drizzle ORM beta (v1.x) | ORM/version policy for backend persistence. |
| **ADR-006** | LangSmith Studio dev routes | Development-only LangSmith/LangGraph debugging routes embedded in the backend when enabled. |
| **ADR-007** | Remove Cloudflare Workers runtime | Backend deployment/runtime must not target Cloudflare Workers; Bun/container model remains. |
| **ADR-008** | Codesearch service and Zoekt orchestration | Backend owns repository schema and Drizzle migrations; codesearch mirrors schema and performs narrow indexing lifecycle updates. |
| **ADR-010** | OpenCypher graph DB and FalkorDB as default | Graph-storage standard the backend must integrate with. |
| **ADR-011** | Backend observability via OpenTelemetry and evlog | OTEL-first telemetry, configurable OTLP endpoints, collector-based fan-out, structured logging, and LLM observability. |
| **ADR-012** | PostgreSQL 17 for Neon compatibility | Database version/managed-host compatibility baseline. |
| **ADR-015** | Docker Compose profiles and small-scale container deploy | Current local/deployment Compose topology; supersedes ADR-004. |
| **ADR-016** | Code-ingestion ReAct agents — recursion limits and context middleware | Constraints and middleware approach for backend code-ingestion agent workflows. |
| **ADR-017** | Amplitude analytics (UI + backend) | Backend/MCP server-side analytics, user/org attribution, non-blocking event emission, and environment configuration. |
| **ADR-018** | Unified `connections` table | Backend data-model standard for provider connections. |
| **ADR-019** | Confluence / Forge self-host, per-org Atlassian 3LO, and provision pipeline | Backend integration/auth and provisioning behavior for Confluence. |
| **ADR-022** | Linear connector Git-native mirror | Backend connector/integration behavior for Linear. |
| **ADR-023** | Notion connector Git-native mirror | Backend connector/integration behavior for Notion. |
| **ADR-024** | Markdown-only local memory capture | Replaces the prior local agent-memory hybrid design; affects backend/local-memory workflows. |
| **ADR-025** | Slack connector Git-native mirror | Backend connector/integration behavior for Slack. |
| **ADR-027** | Codesearch OpenWorkflow concurrency | Backend-facing orchestration/concurrency constraints for codesearch workflows. |
| **ADR-028** | Git-native connector assets | Shared connector asset/storage conventions that backend integrations must follow. |
| **ADR-029** | Railway compute in US East next to Neon | Managed backend deployment region and Postgres connectivity behavior. |
| **ADR-030** | Organization-owned MCP API keys | Backend MCP credential ownership and handling. |
| **ADR-031** | GitHub PR-scoped mirror | Backend GitHub connector/mirroring scope. |
| **ADR-032** | Path-located graph edges | Backend graph data-model/location convention. |
| **ADR-033** | Graph ontology v2 | Backend graph model/ontology standard. |
| **ADR-034** | PagerDuty connector Git-native mirror | Backend connector/integration behavior for PagerDuty. |

**Superseded ADRs — historical only**

- **ADR-004 — Local development with Docker Compose:** superseded by ADR-015.
- **ADR-005 — LangGraph + LangChain integration:** superseded; ADR-006 is the current LangSmith development-route decision.
- **ADR-021 — Local agent memory hybrid MCP proxy:** superseded by ADR-024.

**Codebase (tool-grounded)**

- ADR-002 explicitly establishes the backend as a Hono application on Bun with PostgreSQL/Drizzle, Better Auth, collocated Zod validation, and an integrated MCP interface at `apps/backend`.
- The ADR index at `.ai/memory/decisions/index.md` is the authoritative catalog for ADR status; architectural work should treat accepted, non-superseded decisions above as controlling.
